samples.summary: `collectStale` deletes entries with `purge()`, which never marks the key `evicted` — an entry taken from under a live client then fails silently on every later append
samples.evidence: `collectStale` (line 1136-1138) calls `await this.purge(docKey)`. `purge()` (line 827-835) deletes snapshot/header/changes and does NOT add the key to `this.evicted`. Every other delete-under-a-live-client path deliberately does: `purgeDocument` line 899 (`this.evicted.add(key)`), `dropAllForUser` line ~1060, `evictOldest` (`this.evicted.add(victim)`). Without the marking, `appendChange` finds no header, takes the contractual "no base" silent-success branch (line 633-635 returns false, then `refuseIfEvicted` is a no-op), so every subsequent edit for that document goes nowhere while the chip still reports `Saved to this device` — the exact failure the file's own comments say eviction is careful to avoid. The `isLive` guard at line 1132 is not sufficient to prevent this: it is asked through `isOpenElsewhere`, which `OfflineRuntime` supplies with `whenUnknown: false` (offline-runtime.tsx:~78), so a single failed/unavailable `navigator.locks.query()` answers "not open" and a 30-day-idle-but-open document is collected silently.

samples.summary: Logout erase races the still-mounted durable client: writes are only denied after the erase completes, so the open document can be re-persisted onto the disk the sign-out just cleared
samples.evidence: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` awaits `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` (line 244) and only calls `denyOfflineWrites(who)` at line 256, after it returns. During the erase the durable client's `isPersistenceEnabled` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:172 — `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled() && isOfflineWritePermitted(userId)`) is still true, because the preference is on and the denial has not been recorded. `dropAllForUser` enumerates its key list once up front (`headerKeysWhere(BY_USER, …)`, line 1049) and then purges each in a loop, so a `saveSnapshot`/`appendChange` that lands after the enumeration re-creates a key the loop will never revisit. The result is that the currently-open document's content survives a deliberate sign-out on a shared device — the one promise this module exists to keep. `denyOfflineWrites` (and ideally the `evicted` marking) needs to happen before the erase begins, not after it.

samples.summary: `collectStale` sweeps every account's entries but asks a liveness question scoped to the current account, so another account's open document can be collected out from under it
samples.evidence: `collectStale` deliberately collects entries "whoever wrote them" (comment at line 1106-1113; `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` is unscoped). Liveness is decided by `isLive` → `this.isOpenElsewhere`, which `OfflineRuntime` builds as `isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })` (offline-runtime.tsx). `isOpenInAnyTab` matches lock names with prefix `wb-durable:${userId}:` (durable-session.ts), so a lock held by a *different* account for that document never matches and the entry reads as idle. Combined with the missing `evicted` marking on `purge`, a second account's 30-day-idle-but-open document is deleted and its later appends silently discarded. The sweep's scope and the liveness check's scope have to agree.

samples.summary: `purgeDocument`'s `skipOpen`/`updatedSince` guards protect only the live entries; the archive half is dropped unconditionally
samples.evidence: Lines 885-901 apply `options.skipOpen` and `options.updatedSince` per live key, then line 902-904 calls `dropArchivesForDocument(documentId)` with neither guard. The only caller that passes those options is `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:401-405), which deletes on an *absence* from a listing taken at `listedAt`. An archive written by another tab after the listing — the only copy of work the SDK already gave up reconciling — is therefore deleted even though the equivalent live entry would have been spared. `dropArchivesForDocument` has `row.archivedAt` available and does not consult it.

samples.summary: The durable client's `WafflebaseDocStore` is never closed, leaking an IndexedDB connection for every document opened in a session
samples.evidence: `const store = useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` at line 135-176. There is no `useEffect` cleanup calling `store.close()` anywhere in the file — grepping `close()` across packages/frontend/src returns only offline-runtime.tsx:166, offline-erase.ts (4 sites) and the store's own internals/tests. Each mount of a durable document creates a fresh store object and opens a fresh IDB connection that stays open for the life of the page; navigating between documents accumulates them. Open connections also block `deleteDatabase`/version upgrades from other tabs (the code relies on `onversionchange` to step aside, which only masks it).

`const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` (line 458) then `void eraseOfflineData(current, who).catch(...)` (line 466). When the fallback branch is taken — which the comments say is the ordinary case, since Settings is its own route with no editor mounted — the freshly constructed store's IDB connection is never closed, unlike every other store constructed in this module (lines 263, 295, 329, 412 all close in a `finally`).

samples.summary: `standDown` performs a side effect (`session.release()`) inside a `setState` updater
samples.evidence: `setDecision((current) => { if (!current?.session) return current; current.session.release(); return { subject: current.subject }; })` at lines 236-244. React may invoke an updater more than once (StrictMode, re-render/rebase), so the release can run twice. `acquireDurableSession`'s handle guards with a per-caller `released` flag so the second call is a no-op today, but the impure updater makes the correctness of the release depend on that guard rather than on the call site. Releasing outside the updater would be equivalent and non-reentrant.

samples.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments` wraps the whole loop in one try, so a failure on the first id abandons every remaining id
samples.evidence: Lines 320-328: the `for (const id of documentIds) await store.purgeDocument(...)` loop is inside a single `try`, and the `catch` logs and returns. A transient failure on the first document leaves the local copies of every later document in the batch in place — relevant for `deleteDocuments`, which passes the whole server-confirmed `deleted` array (api/documents.ts:214). `retryPendingOfflineErase`, by contrast, deliberately keeps going per-id.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described: collectStale (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1136-1138) purges aged keys via purge(), and purge() (:827-835) deletes snapshot/header/changes without adding the key to this.evicted — unlike purgeDocument (:899), dropAllForUser (:1071) and evictOldest (:1386), which all mark deliberately and document why. Without the mark, a subsequent appendChange finds no header (:633-635), takes the contractual silent-success branch, and refuseIfEvicted (:711-714) is a no-op, so later edits vanish while durability is still reported. The isLive check at :1132 does not make this unreachable: OfflineRuntime passes whenUnknown:false (offline-runtime.tsx:71-76), and isOpenInAnyTab returns false when navigator.locks.query is missing or throws (durable-session.ts:231-238, 239/257), while supportsDurableSession only requires navigator.locks.request (durable-session.ts:57-66) — so a runtime can hold a durable client and still be reported not-open. There is also a check-then-purge window between :1130-1135 and :1136-1138. Real correctness gap with silent data-loss impact; no named refutation ground applies.

finding.evidence: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` awaits `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` (line 244) and only calls `denyOfflineWrites(who)` at line 256, after it returns. verdict.reason: Verified in the repository. `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` awaits `eraseOfflineData(store, who)` at offline-erase.ts:244 and calls `denyOfflineWrites(who)` only at offline-erase.ts:256, after the erase completes. During the whole erase `isOfflineWritePermitted` (offline-erase.ts:137-139, backed by the `erased` set populated only by `denyOfflineWrites`) still returns true, so the mounted durable client's gate `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled() && isOfflineWritePermitted(userId)` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:172-173) permits writes; the gate is evaluated per write via `refuseIfDisabled` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:382-390, called at saveSnapshot:581, appendChange:623, saveMeta:670), not cached. `dropAllForUser` enumerates its key list once at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1049 and then purges in an awaited loop (1050-1072), so a header re-created after enumeration is never revisited. The re-persist path is concrete: `evicted` is shared per-database across instances (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:189-198, 343-345), so the erase marks the open doc, the client's next `appendChange` throws via `refuseIfEvicted` (654, 711-720), and the SDK's repair `saveSnapshot` (580-600) re-puts the snapshot+header and clears the mark at 598. The flow is live during the window: api/auth.ts:135 awaits the erase before redirecting at 142-144, with the editor still mounted. No guard elsewhere closes this window; ordering (deny before erase) is the fix. In-lane as an async ordering/race defect leaving the invariant "sign-out leaves nothing behind" broken.

finding.summary: `stoodDown` is latched per-subject and never reset, so a document that once stood down stays permanently non-durable while still holding the election lock
finding.evidence:
`const [stoodDown, setStoodDown] = useState<string | null>(null)` (line 239) is written only by `giveUp` (line 241) and read at line 250 (`stoodDown !== subject`). Grepping the whole frontend for `setStoodDown` finds exactly one call site — there is no reset when `subject` changes or when the document re-mounts.

Consequence: after `onLockRefused` fires for subject S (`7:note-7`), the user navigates to another document and back to `note-7`. `held.current` is re-latched for S (line 246-248), and `useDurableDocument`'s effect re-runs for the new/old docKey and **re-acquires** the `wb-durable:7:note-7` Web Lock (use-durable-document.ts:192-221, which has no memory of the stand-down — `standDown` only mutated `decision`, not `latched`/`eligible`). But `decided` is `undefined` because `stoodDown === subject` is still true from the first visit, so `CollabDocumentProvider` returns `inner` (line 305-307) and never mounts `DurableYorkieProvider`.

That is exactly the state this feature's own test asserts must not happen (`collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` → "takes no election it is not going to use": "Holding `wb-durable:{user}:{docKey}` without mounting a client denies durability to every other tab for nothing"). Here the lock is held for the life of the open document, and no other tab can be the durable one for it, while this tab persists nothing.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. collab-document-provider.tsx:239 declares `stoodDown` state; the only writer is `giveUp` (241), and it is read at 250 to null out `decided`. There is no reset on subject/docKey change and no remount forced (NotesDetail at notes-detail.tsx:376-393 renders CollabDocumentProvider with a changing `docKey` under route `/n/:id` (App.tsx:174) while the cached `["me"]` query keeps the component mounted, so useState survives a note->note->note navigation). Meanwhile useDurableDocument has no memory of the stand-down: `standDown` (use-durable-document.ts:235-245) only clears `decision.session`, while `latched`/`eligible` (166-171) and the acquisition effect (192-221, deps include docKey/subject) re-run and re-take the Web Lock via acquireDurableSession (durable-session.ts:139-187). Result on return to the stood-down document: election/Web Lock held with `durable===true` in the hook, but CollabDocumentProvider returns `inner` (305-307) and never mounts DurableYorkieProvider — lock held for nothing, other tabs denied durability, and lapse mis-reported as "another-tab" (257-265). onLockRefused is a real runtime path (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:299-313). Broken invariant / stale-state bug on a reachable path; no guard makes it unreachable.

finding.summary: A `['me','optional']` refetch that resolves to `null` (expired session) tears down the durable subtree and remounts `DocumentProvider`, discarding the in-memory Yorkie change queue the feature exists to protect
finding.evidence:
Line 305: `if (!decided?.durable || !decided.clientKey || !me) return inner;`. `me` comes from `useQuery({queryKey:['me','optional'], queryFn: fetchMeOptional, retry:false})` (line 185-192), and `fetchMeOptional` resolves `null` when there is no valid session (api/auth.ts:171 "Returns null when there is no valid session").

React Query refetches on window focus by default. If the cookie expires while an editor sits open with unsent edits, the refetch resolves `null`, `me` becomes null, and two things happen at once: `subject` (line 233) flips from `7:note-7` to `anon:note-7`, re-latching `held.current` with `durable:false`, and the `!me` term short-circuits to `return inner`. `inner` is a *different element type at the same position* than the `<DurableYorkieProvider>{inner}</DurableYorkieProvider>` branch, so React unmounts `DocumentProvider` and the whole editor under it.

The file's own doc comment (lines 208-222) states this is precisely the loss the latch exists to prevent: "switching between them unmounts the `DocumentProvider` and the entire editor subtree under it — discarding the Yorkie change queue, which on a document with unsent edits is the loss this whole feature exists to prevent." The latch handles a preference flip but not `me → null`. A *different* user signing in is a deliberate re-decide; a session simply expiring is not, and there is no guard distinguishing them.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository, and the finding is accurate as described. collab-document-provider.tsx:305 is literally `if (!decided?.durable || !decided.clientKey || !me) return inner;`. `me` comes from useQuery(['me','optional'], fetchMeOptional) at lines 185-192, and api/auth.ts:167-184 confirms fetchMeOptional resolves `null` when the 401 refresh fails. App.tsx:89 constructs `new QueryClient()` with no defaultOptions, so refetchOnWindowFocus defaults to true and staleTime is 0 — a focus refetch after session expiry overwrites the seeded initialData with null. When that happens, `subject` (line 233) moves from `{id}:{docKey}` to `anon:{docKey}`; use-durable-document.ts:127-132/166-171/254 make `eligible` false and `settled` true immediately for the new identity, so `ready` is true, the pre-decision gate at line 301 does not hold, the latch is rewritten at line 247 with `durable:false`, and line 305 returns bare `inner` — a different element type at the same position as the `<DurableYorkieProvider>` branch (309-328), which unmounts DocumentProvider and the editor subtree. That is exactly the loss the file's own doc comments at 208-222 and 291-296 say the latch exists to prevent. The existing tests cover a different user signing in (durable test 167-193) and a preference flip (196-228) but not me -> null, and I found no guard distinguishing a deliberate account switch from a session simply expiring. Data loss (discarded in-memory Yorkie change queue) on a reachable path is squarely in the correctness lane and graded critical by impact; the opt-in precondition narrows reach but does not refute it.

finding.summary: `purgeDocument`'s archive drop ignores the `skipOpen` and `updatedSince` guards, so the reconcile can delete an archive — the only copy of unreconciled work — for a document its own guards just spared
finding.evidence:
In `purgeDocument` (lines 885-905) the `skipOpen` and `updatedSince` checks are inside the per-live-entry loop (lines 886-892), but `if (options.archives === "drop") { await this.dropArchivesForDocument(documentId); }` (line 902) runs unconditionally afterwards, outside both guards.

`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:401-405) calls it with `{archives:'drop', skipOpen:true, updatedSince: listedAt}` for every id absent from a listing taken a moment ago. So a document that is `isLive` in another tab, or whose entry was touched after `listedAt`, keeps its live entry but loses its archive. An archive is by this feature's own design the only durable copy of work the SDK could not reconcile (offline-copy.ts header comment), so the loss is unrecoverable. The guards were added precisely because the listing's absence is a guess, not an answer — the same reasoning applies to the archive, which is the more valuable of the two.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository: in `purgeDocument` the `skipOpen` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:886) and `updatedSince` (887-892) checks are `continue`s inside the per-live-entry loop that closes at line 901, while the archive drop at 902-904 runs unconditionally on `options.archives === "drop"` alone. `dropArchivesForDocument` (959-975) applies no liveness/recency filter either, deleting every matching archive row for the user despite `archivedAt` being stored (line 93). The path is reachable in normal use: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:401-405) passes `{archives:"drop", skipOpen:true, updatedSince:listedAt}` for every id in `revoked`, a set that by design includes ids known only via archives (storedDocumentIds({archives:true}), line 396) — for those the guarded loop iterates zero times yet the archive is still destroyed; offline-runtime.tsx:133-139 invokes this once per session with listedAt stamped before fetchDocuments and isOpenElsewhere supplied, which is exactly the shared-database/other-tab race the guards were added for (documented offline-erase.ts:360-367, wafflebase-doc-store.ts:859-867). An archive is by the module's own documentation (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:847-857) the only durable copy of work the SDK could not reconcile, so the deletion is unrecoverable data loss. No guard elsewhere covers it, and the cleanup tests (wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:725-767) assert only live-entry sparing, never archive survival under skipOpen/updatedSince. Real, reachable, data-loss — blocking under the correctness rubric.
